thread.title: Guardians rally from 2‑0 deficit to force Game 5 in ALDS
thread.title_full: Guardians rally from 2‑0 deficit to force Game 5 in ALDS

author: mercnews
title: Guardians rally from 2‑0 deficit to force Game 5 in ALDS
text:
José Ramírez's power surge propels Cleveland to a 9‑5 win over Chicago, forcing a winner‑take‑all game. Gavin Williams closes the series for the first time in his career.
On Thursday evening, the Cleveland Guardians captured a decisive 9-5 victory over the Chicago White Sox in Game 4 of the American League Division Series, pushing the series into a winner‑take‑all Game 5.
The Guardians' win was built on several key offensive explosions and a defensive effort that stifled the White Sox's comeback hopes. The game's turning point began in the fifth inning when José Ramírez delivered a two‑run homer off a 99.9‑mph fastball that sent the ball deep to right‑center. Ramírez, a seven‑time All‑Star who had just returned from surgery, had already endured a 26‑game stretch without an RBI.
Guardians Erase Deficit With Key Home Runs
His blast was the first of what would be three runs for the Guardians, helping to lift them from a 2‑0 deficit. The same inning saw pinch hitter Patrick Bailey lead off with a home run that opened the scoreboard for Cleveland, followed by a single from Steven Kwan that chased the White Sox's closer Erick Fedde to the bullpen.
Chicago's pitching had looked strong at the start of the series, but it unraveled in the sixth as Grant Taylor struggled. After pitching five scoreless innings in the first two meetings, Taylor allowed four runs in less than an inning, giving up a hitless rally that lifted the Guardians to a 6‑3 lead.
The White Sox responded in the bottom of the sixth, with Sam Antonacci driving in two runs on a hit‑by‑pitch from Tim Herrin that loaded the bases, and Brenton Doyle harvesting a sacrifice fly that pushed the score to 6‑4. Yet Cleveland's staging continued unabated; a run‑scoring single from Ramírez followed by another run blade pushed the game to 9‑5 before the White Sox could mount a counter‑offensive.
Williams Secures Victory In Relief Appearance
Like the Guardians' offense, the game ended on a spectacular pitching performance by Cleveland's bullpen. Reliever Gavin Williams closed the game with his debut relief appearance, striking out the side in the ninth and recording the final three outs after Miguel Vargas had already arrived home on a solo homer for the White Sox earlier in the inning.
Williams, who had never pitched in relief in the majors until that night, provided the Guardians with the needed finality for Game 4 and remains a potential starter for Game 5. Overall, the Guardians collected 15 hits, including five homers, and outgained the White Sox 9‑5, while their pitching staff limited the White Sox to five runs over nine innings.
Chicago, meanwhile, saw veteran Miguel Vargas hit a homer and Sam Antonacci contribute two RBIs, but could not overcome the momentum shift that began in the fifth. Currently, Cleveland is one win away from becoming the first major‑league club to rally from a 2‑0 series deficit in a best‑of‑five matchup, achieving what the 2017 New York Yankees had done against them.
Cleveland Poised To Force Historic Game 5
If the Guardians can maintain their offensive firepower and bullpen reliability, they look poised to force a Game 5 that could cap off one of the most remarkable comeback narratives in recent postseason history. With 39,920 fans in attendance, the game delivered high drama and set the stage for a possible historic series conclusion.
The Guardians now head into the final game with a chance to write history while the White Sox look to salvage a postseason appearance their fans will remember.
